title: Pacing and skipping
summary: Checkpoints for both test formats, a two-pass approach that banks the easy points first, and the four ways time leaks away.

slides.title: Not every question gets the same time
body: Logical Reasoning questions get harder through the section, so an even pace is the wrong pace. Move quickly through the early questions to bank time for the last ten.
Every question is worth one point. A question that eats four minutes costs you the two easy ones at the end you never reach.
slides.callout: First ten at about 54 seconds, next five at 72, the rest at 108, with two minutes to spare.

slides.note: Behind at a checkpoint by more than a minute? Skip the next long, dense question on sight and come back to it last.

Per passage

slides.note: Skimming saves time on the read and loses more on every question. Read properly once.

steps.label: First pass
steps.do: Answer every question you can see into. If you can’t see a way in within about ten seconds, flag it and move on.

steps.label: Return pass
steps.do: Go back to the flagged questions, easiest-looking first, hardest last.

steps.label: Never leave a blank
steps.do: There is no penalty for a wrong answer. With 30 seconds left, fill every blank.

steps.label: Practise the decision
steps.do: The skip trainer grades your attempt-or-skip choices so the habit is automatic on test day.

traps.name: The bleed
traps.tell: One question you refuse to leave. Set a mental limit of about two minutes; past it, pick your best guess, flag, move.

traps.name: Answer ping-pong
traps.tell: Bouncing between two choices without new information. Go back to the stimulus for the word that decides it, or flag.

traps.name: Rereading loop
traps.tell: Rereading a sentence hoping it will make sense. Paraphrase what you can and keep going; the rest of the paragraph usually explains it.

traps.name: Skim reading
traps.tell: Saving a minute on the passage and losing twenty seconds on each of seven questions.

slides.title: Cheat card
lines: Fast early, slow late; two minutes of buffer at the end.
RC: about 8:30 a passage, at least 3:30 of it reading.
Can’t see in within ten seconds? Flag and move.
